'''Cliftonville Football & Athletic Club''' is a professional association football club playing in the [[NIFL Premiership]] – the top division of the [[Northern Ireland Football League]]. The club was founded on 20 September 1879 by [[John McAlery]] in the suburb of [[Cliftonville, Belfast|Cliftonville]] in north [[Belfast]] and are the founders of football in [[Ireland]].

It is the oldest [[association football|football]] club in [[Ireland]] and celebrated its 140th anniversary in 2019. Since 1890, the club has played home matches at [[Solitude (football ground)|Solitude]]. Cliftonville contests the [[North Belfast derby]] with nearby rivals [[Crusaders F.C.|Crusaders]], and also has local rivalries with [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]] and [[Glentoran F.C.|Glentoran]]. They have the distinction of [[List of unrelegated association football clubs|never being relegated]], along with the [[Big Two derby|Big Two]].

The club has won the [[NIFL Premiership#Champions|league title]] five times outright including one shared title, the [[Irish Cup]] nine times and the [[Northern Ireland Football League Cup]] six times."}}
